content.text:
`saveAll` was resolving early because it used `items.forEach(async …)`. `forEach` ignores the promises its callback returns, so the function returned the count before any write finished. A failed write also went unnoticed instead of rejecting.

In `store.js` it now does `await Promise.all(items.map((item) => db.put(item.id, item)))` before returning the count. It resolves only after every write completes, and it rejects if any write fails. The writes run in parallel, as they did before. If your db needs them in order, say so and I'll switch to a sequential loop.

I added two tests to `test/store.test.js`. One uses a slow `put` to check that `saveAll` waits for it. The other checks that a failing `put` makes `saveAll` reject.
